summary: Extensions should make the pipeline discoverable, gate transitions with executable evidence, and preserve durable rationale when the normal path is overridden.

items.text: Publish a concise pipeline entry point beside the workflow code: task class, graph, artifacts, tool scopes, budgets, and the command for a local dry run.
Attach machine-checkable contracts to every handoff and require the safety-net result before a pipeline can advance from implementation to review.
Add a bounded exception edge: unresolved or high-impact failures leave a decision record and escalate to a named human rather than looping or silently accepting.

See Continuous Two-Way Alignment for the related use case or counterpoint: Continuously reconcile system artifacts and their human-facing companion in both directions so neither machine progress nor human knowledge becomes an isolated, drifting truth.

See On-the-Fly Generated UIs (Usually Cached) for the related use case or counterpoint: Generate an interface from the artifact it fronts, cache and version the result against those inputs, and regenerate it when they change.
See Agent as a Process Actor for the related use case or counterpoint: Let agents own bounded process steps, never ambiguous process state.

See Skip the Pull Request for the related use case or counterpoint: In agent-first delivery, gates in front of the integration merge replace the human pull-request review — the operator reads verdicts, not diffs.

See Switching Abstraction Layers for the related use case or counterpoint: Move from code and prompts to tasks, pipelines, reviews and capacity only when evidence makes the lower layer trustworthy enough to manage by signals.
See Agent-Workforce Management for the related use case or counterpoint: Manage agents like a workforce — roles, costs, allowances, escalation paths.
